name: Photography is an Art of Observation: Learn to see
description: Photography is an art of observation. Learn to notice light, gestures and relationships, then use framing, timing and technique to express what matters.

step.name: Minutes 1–2: notice your first response.
step.text: Minutes 1–2: notice your first response. What caught your attention? Identify a subject, detail or feeling that might give you a reason to make a photograph. Keep the camera down while you explore the wider scene.

step.name: Minutes 3–4: follow the light.
step.text: Minutes 3–4: follow the light. Look at where light and shadow fall. Notice reflections, bright patches and changes in colour. Watch whether the light strengthens your initial idea or draws you elsewhere.

step.name: Minutes 5–6: look for relationships.
step.text: Minutes 5–6: look for relationships. Notice how shapes, spaces and subjects connect. Does a small change in your position separate overlapping elements, reveal a pattern or give your subject more room?

step.name: Minutes 7–8: watch for change.
step.text: Minutes 7–8: watch for change. Follow movement and repeated behaviour. A person may enter a useful space, a breeze may change a reflection, or a cloud may alter the balance of light. Decide what would make you ready to press the shutter.

step.name: Minutes 9–10: choose your response.
step.text: Minutes 9–10: choose your response. Does your first idea still interest you? If it does, raise the camera and refine the frame. If something else now matters more, follow that. You can also finish the exercise without making a photograph.
